data.narrative:
SpectralX is a Series A defense and security technology company founded by Asaf Picciotto and former IDF special-forces veterans. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 10 same-sector companies at Series A and adjacent stages, comprising 8 private firms and 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). Notable private peers include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Singularity, and NODA AI.

The peer-median method, the applicable triangulation approach given available data, anchors on a median valuation of $1.0B across the 10-company sample. The peer range spans $125M at the floor to $3.0B at the ceiling, with representative data points including Dream Security at $3.0B (Series B), Harmattan AI at $1.4B (Series B), Code Metal at $1.2B (Series B), and Castelion and Defense Unicorns each at $1.0B (Series B). This peer-median result reflects typical market pricing for well-capitalized, technical teams operating in the defense sector at this stage.

The triangulated valuation range is $850M to $1.1B, with a midpoint of $1.0B. Key uncertainties include the magnitude of SpectralX's product differentiation relative to the peer set, the company's current burn rate and runway post-Series A, and the specific defensibility of its technical approach within an increasingly crowded frontier-defense market. A single-method analysis limits conviction; additional data on comparable transaction multiples or revenue run-rate would strengthen the assessment.
